verdict: The proposal provides a robust and well-considered read-only UX transition, effectively managing the mental model shift for operators.
summary: Proposal 031 r10 successfully resolves previous UX concerns by replacing disabled primary buttons with clear diagnostic banners and introducing a first-run orientation banner. This aligns the operator's mental model with the new read-only state of the application. The task flow for accessing external write paths is explicitly managed, and the accessibility guidelines for VoiceOver ensure the diagnostic states are understandable. The explicit placement of the syncing pattern and report payload indicators provides necessary visual stability and feedback.

non_blocking_issues.description: The exact external workflows (CLI/MCP commands) for the operator write-path guide are currently undefined (OQ-031-01). If these external workflows are too complex or disjointed, the overall task flow will still experience high user friction despite the clear in-app diagnostic guidance.

suggestions.description: Ensure the first-run onboarding banner's link to the operator guide is directly clickable or easily copyable, minimizing the friction of context switching to the external tool.
For VoiceOver accessibility on the Reports list, ensure the payload availability state is read as a complete sentence (e.g., 'Report payload is currently generating') to avoid ambiguity.

assumptions: Operators are familiar with or can easily learn the external CLI/MCP tools referenced in the write-path guide.
The diagnostic identifiers provided in the UI (run_id, stage_id, etc.) match exactly what the external CLI/MCP tools expect as input arguments.
